I'd noticed the soap dispensers at work now pump out a highly aerated foam, instead of the previous dollop of liquid and realized it was a canny cost saving move on the part of the janitorial company that services the dispenser. As a foam, there's less soap being dispensed, hence lass cost and likely less waste.

It was then that I realized I could do the same thing with my pricey Dr. Bronner's soap.

I decanted half of a new bottle into the empty I'd just finished with. I stored one bottle and put the other in the shower. When it came time I shook the bottle vigorously for about 15-30 seconds, it was full of extremely fine bubbles, much like the dispenser soap at work. I squeezed out a dollop between the size of a quarter and a half dollar into my cupped hand and lathered my entire body.

After a week, I couldn't see any appreciable drop in the level of soap remaining. After a month, yeah. I'm thinking this half bottle could last me a year or more, where previously I was going through it every six months or so.
LPT: Make your expensive liquid soap last longer
You can buy a product that says it can save 75% of your daily soap used and its only $15. Just so you dont have to shake vigorously before you pump. http://www.amazon.com/gp/aw/d/B001RRG5VI?vs=1
Thanks for the link, but with 36% 2 stars or less from 452 customer reviews, I think I'll stick with shaking for now. :D

You can also just buy a $2 bottle of foaming soap and reuse the bottle. Or, you can buy a foam pump bottle that has better reviews. If you really wanna get crunchy you can use the unscented Dr. Bronner's and add your own essential oils. They do wear out eventually because the foam is created by pushing the liquid through a fine mesh to aerate it. If the mesh gets clogged it can blow out the seals on the pump. Running a bottle full of plain hot water through the pump between fillings seems to help as does using filtered water if your water is hard.
